# 008: Phase 6 validation harness and baselines

**Date:** 2026-10-25
**Phase:** 6 (gate G2)
**Affects:** `configs/models.yaml`, `configs/regions.yaml`
**Report:** `reports/baselines.md` (generated by `uv run heatwave evaluate-baselines`)

## What was built

- **Walk-forward runner** (`validation/walk_forward.py`). Per fold:
  - training rows are those whose target year is in the fold's training years, in the training window (15 Feb – 15 Aug);
  - scored rows are those in the fold's validation years with valid dates in the evaluation season (March–July). For the window target, all ten valid dates must be in the season.
  - Before anything is fitted, the runner checks that training years end before validation years and that the fold climatology was fitted on training years only.
  - The 5 folds pool into out-of-fold (OOF) predictions for **2006–2020** (15 years), saved to `data/oof/`. Phase 7 calibrates on them.
- **Metrics** (`validation/metrics.py`):
  - Brier skill score against M0; ROC-AUC and PR-AUC, with the base rate and M0 beside them;
  - reliability tables and the Brier decomposition;
  - a **year-block bootstrap**: 2,000 resamples of whole validation years, all districts together. It is paired, so every model is scored on the same resampled years, and it is computed exactly from per-year sums.
- **Breakdowns:** by lead, the **onset subset** (no heatwave day in the 3 days up to t), the window target, valid month, region and year.
- **Regions** (`configs/regions.yaml`): UP's four standard economic regions, Western 30, Central 10, Eastern 28, Bundelkhand 7. **Confirmed by the owner.**
- **Baselines** (`models/baselines.py`), per-lead and window versions:
  - **M0:** climatological heatwave frequency (fold climatology).
  - **M1:** persistence lookup over heatwave-at-t × Tmax-anomaly bin (8) × season band (Feb–Apr, May–Jun, Jul–Aug) × lead, shrunk toward climatology (pseudo-count 20). The season band was added to reference.md §4.4's specification, because the same anomaly means different things in March and May.
  - **M2:** logistic regression, **one model per lead**, so each feature's weight can fade with lead. Inputs: doy sin/cos, Tmax anomaly, 7-day mean anomaly, root-zone soil-moisture anomaly, logit of the climatological frequency; standardised; L2 with C = 1.

## Results (OOF 2006–2020, March–July)

| | Lead 1 | Lead 4 | Lead 7 | Lead 10 | Window (10 days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 BSS | +0.037 [+0.008, +0.069] | −0.004 | −0.013 | −0.020 | +0.038 [−0.004, +0.084] |
| **M2 BSS** | **+0.052 [+0.023, +0.084]** | +0.020 [+0.005, +0.036] | +0.015 [+0.002, +0.029] | +0.015 [+0.002, +0.031] | **+0.095 [+0.051, +0.150]** |
| M2 BSS, onsets | +0.051 [+0.033, +0.077] | +0.030 | +0.016 | +0.014 [+0.007, +0.024] | +0.074 [+0.043, +0.116] |
| ROC-AUC: M0 / M2 | 0.747 / 0.869 | 0.747 / 0.825 | 0.747 / 0.799 | 0.747 / 0.789 | 0.735 / 0.819 |

- **M2 beats climatology at every lead,** with intervals above 0. The skill horizon, the last lead whose interval excludes 0, is **10**, for all issue dates and for onsets. "Lead 1" is already 4 days after the newest data (L = 3).
- **M2 beats M1 at every lead** (paired interval excludes 0). M1 beats climatology only at lead 1, because its cells pool districts and lose climatology's district-and-date detail.
- **By region (M2):** central +0.032, eastern +0.025, western +0.018, Bundelkhand +0.020 [−0.001, +0.038] (weakest).
- **Under-forecasting the hot 2010s:** observed rate 4.3 % vs M2 mean 3.0 % and M0 3.0 % over 2006–2020. Validation blocks swing widely, from 0.8 % (2006–08) to 7.3 % (2012–14). Phase 7's calibration and the sliding-vs-expanding window test address this.

## Gate G2: pass, after a check redesign (recorded)

The first run failed one check: "M0's mean forecast within 30 % of the observed rate". Pooled 2006–2020, M0 was 31 % low.

That check was intended to catch a **computation or date-alignment bug** (the failure G2 exists for), but it compared M0 against *held-out* years. Honest climatology is expected to miss those when they are hotter than the training years, and 2010–2014 were. The check now compares M0 with **its own training rows**: within 0.2 % in every fold, so M0 is computed correctly. The out-of-sample comparison stays in the report as information. Changing a check after seeing its result needs this record; the evidence that it was a design flaw is that the in-sample rates match to within 0.2 %.

**The owner accepted the redesigned check.** Final G2 checks, all passed:
- M1 and M2 lead-1 intervals above 0;
- skill falls from lead 1 to lead 10 for M1 and M2;
- M0 matches its training-row rate in every fold.
